title: Understand what GenAI can and cannot do
statement: I need to understand the limits of GenAI so that I can decide whether it is suitable for my task.
success: The user can explain relevant capabilities and limitations without assuming generated output is reliable.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Introductory explanations occur on several learning surfaces; the contexts differ, but the basic answer can be shared.
action: Reuse one concise basics explanation; preserve contextual learning examples.

title: Know whether I may use AI for this assessment
statement: I need to determine whether a particular AI use is permitted for my assessment so that I do not breach my course requirements.
success: The user obtains an unambiguous owner-approved interpretation and knows which course/assessment instructions apply.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Central student guidance uses an allowed-unless-prohibited default, while faculty and Library wording requires authorisation. More content does not resolve the inconsistency.
owner: Academic integrity office + Senate policy owner
action: Resolve the common answer before consolidation; reuse it everywhere with course-level qualifications.

title: Communicate permitted AI use in my assessment
statement: I need to communicate my assessment AI-use expectations so that students know what assistance is permitted.
success: A student can identify the applicable restrictions and disclosure requirements from the assessment instructions.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Several instructor resources address communicating expectations; faculty examples can support one maintained common framework.
action: Share an approved course-statement framework and retain discipline-specific examples.

title: Explain how AI contributed to my work
statement: I need to disclose the role AI played in my work so that others can judge its provenance and my contribution.
success: The disclosure identifies the assistance used and follows the requirements of the relevant course, research or work context.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Transparency and disclosure are repeated across educational, research and operational contexts; the common concept is shared, but obligations remain scope-specific.
owner: Academic integrity office + Graduate Studies + UIT
action: Provide a shared disclosure entry point with clearly separated course, research and operational requirements.

title: Format a reference to AI-generated material
statement: I need to cite AI-generated material in the required citation style so that my references meet academic expectations.
success: The user can apply the required style to the relevant AI material; citation is not mistaken for permission to use AI.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Multiple Library and skills resources serve the same citation-formatting need.
action: Select one maintained style-guidance destination; make permission and disclosure separate linked needs.

title: Check whether an AI-generated claim is trustworthy
statement: I need to verify an AI-generated claim before relying on it so that inaccurate output does not enter my work.
success: The user can check the claim against suitable independent evidence and recognise when verification is not possible.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Practical verification advice complements general warnings about hallucination and human oversight.
action: Promote practical verification steps instead of repeating warnings without a next action.

title: Check that an AI-generated reference exists
statement: I need to verify a reference suggested by AI so that I do not cite a fabricated or misidentified source.
success: The user locates the actual source and checks its bibliographic details and relevance.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: A specific Library chapter directly addresses fabricated citations; this is distinct from formatting a reference.
action: Expose this as a distinct check in research and citation pathways.

title: Use AI without replacing the learning I need to do
statement: I need to keep developing my own understanding when AI is available so that assistance does not replace the skills my course is meant to build.
success: The user can distinguish supportive learning activity from outsourcing the learning or assessment task.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Student guidance and a faculty checklist discuss critical thinking, dependency and retaining one own contribution.
action: Consolidate common learning advice and retain course-specific practice examples.

title: Decide whether an AI use aligns with my values
statement: I need to assess the ethical implications of a proposed AI use so that I can make an informed choice about using it.
success: The user can identify relevant bias, equity, copyright, accessibility and sustainability considerations for the proposed use.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Ethics material supplies a reflective lens, not a blanket approval or prohibition for every use case.
action: Reuse the ethics lens; keep enforceable rules and use-case approvals distinct.

title: Identify a York-approved tool for my intended task
statement: I need to identify an approved AI tool for my intended task so that I do not assume any publicly available product is authorised.
success: A tool record identifies the specific product/licence, eligibility, scope and applicable approval conditions.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Approved-tool and service lists exist, but task, licence, authentication and data conditions are distributed across pages.
action: Maintain one task-filtered tool register; listing a product must not imply approval for all uses.

title: Determine the classification of information I want to use
statement: I need to classify the information in my task so that I can apply the right AI data-handling restrictions.
success: The user can distinguish public, internal, confidential and regulated information using the authoritative classification definitions.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The formal standard and service guidance explain classifications; the standard is not itself a tool approval matrix.
action: Link the formal definitions from a single data decision guide.

title: Determine whether I may put particular data into a tool
statement: I need to determine whether my information may be entered into a specific AI service so that I do not disclose it through an unsuitable tool.
success: The user can match data class, purpose, licence, sign-in state and configuration to an approved handling rule.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Rules and matrices are present, but not unified; the audit could not establish all visual allow/deny states or live configurations.
action: Publish one accessible, owner-approved decision route with explicit conditions; do not infer permissions from the number of sources.

title: Know what happens to my AI inputs after use
statement: I need to know how my AI inputs are retained or accessed so that I can make an informed privacy decision.
success: The relevant service record provides current retention, access and model-training conditions for the actual licence/configuration.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: UIT and SAVY make privacy statements, including absolute assertions; the audit did not verify current service configurations or vendor conditions.
owner: Privacy office + UIT service owners + Student Services
action: Review each claim against the actual enterprise configuration and publish scoped, dated conditions.

title: Obtain access to an AI tool I am eligible to use
statement: I need an actionable access route for an eligible AI service so that I can start using the sanctioned service.
success: The user can identify the sign-in or request route and any eligibility conditions for the selected service.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Service access routes exist, but some destinations could not be inspected and the routes differ by product.
action: Expose one product-specific access action per tool and verify each destination.

title: Know the cost of the AI licence I need
statement: I need to know the cost and charging basis of a required AI licence so that I can obtain the necessary budget approval.
success: The user can locate current owner-reviewed price, charging period and applicable purchasing conditions for the selected licence.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The services page gives Microsoft 365 Copilot pricing, but this is not a comprehensive or independently price-validated catalogue.
owner: UIT service owners + relevant budget owner
action: Store time-sensitive licence costs in owner-maintained tool records with review dates.

title: Identify which coding-assistant licence is permitted for York work
statement: I need to identify the appropriate coding-assistant licence so that a personal subscription is not mistaken for York enterprise approval.
success: The user distinguishes GitHub Copilot Enterprise from personal GitHub Copilot and from Microsoft 365 Copilot.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Dedicated enterprise service information and the initiative page distinguish institutional and personal licensing.
action: Present the coding product as a distinct catalogue entry with institutional-use conditions.

title: Know whether I may enable an AI assistant in this meeting
statement: I need to determine whether an AI assistant may be enabled in an administrative meeting so that the participants and meeting context are respected.
success: The organiser can apply approval, participant consent and meeting-sensitivity requirements before enabling the assistant.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The administrative supplement addresses this need, but activation guidance is elsewhere and the scope must remain non-academic.
owner: VPFA guideline owner + UIT + privacy office
action: Place the scoped consent checklist directly beside activation instructions.

title: Decline AI capture of an administrative meeting
statement: I need to know what happens if I object to an AI meeting assistant so that my objection can be respected.
success: The participant can identify the administrative guideline requirement that the assistant not be used if any participant objects.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The administrative supplement directly states the effect of an objection; this does not establish a general academic recording rule.
action: Make the objection rule visible to participants before the meeting.

title: Handle an AI-generated meeting summary appropriately
statement: I need to handle an AI meeting summary appropriately so that inaccurate or sensitive meeting information is not distributed carelessly.
success: The organiser can apply the administrative guideline requirements for verifying and sharing the generated summary.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The administrative supplement supplies summary-management guidance; generic product capability descriptions are not a substitute.
owner: VPFA guideline owner + meeting organiser + privacy office
action: Expose the summary-handling instructions in the meeting-assistant task route.

title: Know when my proposed AI use requires oversight
statement: I need to determine the oversight required for a proposed operational AI use so that I do not make a consequential use without appropriate review.
success: The user can distinguish generally permissible, oversight-required and impermissible uses within the guideline scope.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Operational guidelines and initiative examples address the same decision need.
action: Provide one scoped use-case assessment route and link additional specialist requirements.

title: Find how to request approval for a new AI assistant
statement: I need to find the approval route for a proposed new AI assistant so that I do not deploy an unapproved tool.
success: The requester can reach the correct assessment intake and understand the information needed for that request.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The administrative supplement directs users to CTRA, but the intake and its full requirements were not inspected in this audit.
action: Expose the verified intake action and publish a public preparation checklist; confirm scope beyond administrative assistants.

title: Identify the current rule that applies to my AI use
statement: I need to identify the current authoritative rule for my context so that I do not act on a superseded draft or a rule for a different activity.
success: The user can distinguish authority, scope, effective date and historical status of relevant policy or guidance.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Current routes expose differently dated operational documents, and historical academic wording still appears in current guidance.
owner: Relevant policy authorities + central web owner
action: Publish a policy register with explicit scope, authority and supersession confirmed by each owner.

title: Preserve intended learning outcomes in assessment design
statement: I need to design assessment for the presence of AI so that the assessed work still demonstrates the intended learning.
success: The instructor can choose an assessment approach justified by the learning outcomes rather than a blanket assumption about AI.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Commons, central instructor guidance and LA&PS provide overlapping but contextually useful pedagogical resources.
owner: Teaching Commons + academic integrity office + faculty teaching leads
action: Index pedagogical examples by the learning need; reuse common policy guidance.

title: Use AI to prototype a course component
statement: I need to prototype a course component with AI so that I can evaluate a draft before deciding what belongs in my teaching.
success: The instructor can adapt and critically review a relevant example without treating the generated draft as final course content.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The LA&PS toolkit and Commons resources provide practical examples, not just high-level principles.
action: Retain practical examples, tagged to the task and learning context.

title: Express my task effectively in an AI prompt
statement: I need to express my task clearly to an AI tool so that I can critically evaluate a more relevant response.
success: The user can form a prompt with context, goal and constraints appropriate to the task.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: UIT templates, research prompting and course-design examples serve one general skill with different contexts.
action: Share the prompting basics and preserve specialised examples in one indexed collection.

title: Find professional development for teaching with AI
statement: I need to find suitable AI teaching development so that I can improve my educational practice.
success: The user can identify a relevant workshop, course, certificate or self-paced resource and its access route.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Teaching Commons has a dedicated development offer; central and faculty pages can point to it rather than reproduce calendars.
action: Syndicate offerings into a common learning catalogue with format and eligibility.

title: Find AI training relevant to my staff role
statement: I need to identify suitable AI training for my work role so that I can use the tools responsibly.
success: The user can confirm the relevant offering, eligibility and access route.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Public pages name staff and manager packages, but both YU Learn destinations returned HTTP 500 and their contents were not inspected.
action: Verify the destinations and publish useful public abstracts without claiming the training is absent.

title: Agree acceptable AI use in my thesis or dissertation
statement: I need to agree acceptable AI use with my supervisory team so that my thesis or dissertation meets disciplinary expectations.
success: The student and supervisory team establish an explicit understanding before the relevant research or writing activity.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Graduate-specific guidance is present but hosted under the educational site and also referenced by research information.
action: Expose one canonical graduate decision pathway from both teaching and research.

title: Choose a suitable AI scholarly-discovery tool
statement: I need to assess an AI scholarly-discovery tool so that its coverage and limitations suit my research task.
success: The user can assess scholarly coverage, cost and limitations without mistaking a Library description for enterprise approval.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: A dedicated Library workflow chapter supplies the research-task perspective.
action: Keep research-tool evaluation distinct from University data/approval decisions.

title: Determine a funder AI restriction for my proposal
statement: I need to determine the applicable funder rule on AI use in my proposal so that the submission complies with that funder requirements.
success: The researcher locates the current applicable funder statement and knows which part of the proposal process it governs.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: York pages signpost external funder material; those external rules and their current status were not audited.
action: Maintain a dated external-rule signpost with explicit scope; verify external content before summarising it.

title: Find York expertise relevant to my AI research question
statement: I need to find relevant York AI research expertise so that I can identify a suitable collaborator or research environment.
success: The user can identify a relevant centre/lab and follow its authoritative expertise/contact route.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Several directories and centre sites support discovery, but have different disciplinary scopes.
action: Maintain one searchable expertise index while keeping detailed research sites with their owners.

title: Find scholarly sources about AI as a subject
statement: I need to find scholarly literature about AI so that I can investigate an AI-related research question.
success: The user can locate appropriate disciplinary databases, books or journals without confusing this with advice on using AI to do research.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The Library AI subject guide is a distinct answer from the guide to research with GenAI.
action: Label research ON AI separately from research WITH AI.

title: Find an AI-related research funding opportunity
statement: I need to find a relevant AI-related research funding opportunity so that I can assess whether to apply.
success: The user can reach the opportunity owner and verify current eligibility, deadline and application instructions.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Connected Minds supplies opportunity routes, but not every individual funding record was analyst-reviewed and one scholarship destination failed retrieval.
action: Aggregate opportunity metadata from owners; do not infer that a listed call remains open.

title: Find a York degree pathway relevant to my AI goals
statement: I need to identify a suitable AI-related degree pathway so that I can make an informed study choice.
success: The user can reach the programme owner for current curriculum, admission and application requirements.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Multiple MMAI surfaces address the same choice, while a legacy EECS specialisation link no longer lands on the intended programme.
action: Use canonical programme metadata and preserve distinct application journeys.

title: Find an AI-related professional credential
statement: I need to find a suitable AI-related professional credential so that I can develop skills relevant to my work.
success: The user can distinguish programme purpose and confirm current enrolment details with the provider.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: AI Governance and data-learning programmes are described; a Machine Learning programme link returned 404.
action: Keep programme status current; distinguish fee-based credentials from internal staff training and internal policy.

title: Find support to commercialise an AI-related idea
statement: I need to find entrepreneurship support for an AI-related idea so that I can assess a route towards application or commercialisation.
success: The user can identify a relevant support programme and follow its intake/eligibility route.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Research information signposts the existing entrepreneurship ecosystem rather than providing a separate AI-only service.
action: Use a shared innovation-support entry and keep actual service intake at source.

title: Find specialist help for an AI-related IP question
statement: I need to find specialist intellectual-property support for my AI-related work so that I can obtain advice through the appropriate service.
success: The user reaches a qualified service and can check its eligibility and intake, without treating the hub as legal advice.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The IP Innovation Clinic is a specialist destination; general ethics information is not a substitute.
action: Retain the specialist service and publish a clear eligibility-aware pointer.

title: Find AI-use guidance specific to legal research
statement: I need to find discipline-specific AI-use guidance for legal research so that I can apply the relevant professional and academic expectations.
success: The user reaches current law-library guidance appropriate to the jurisdiction and research task.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The York research page describes a relevant law guide, but that destination returned 404. General AI-and-law commentary does not verify replacement guidance.
owner: Osgoode law library + Research & Innovation web owner
action: Confirm the intended replacement with the law library; do not declare the underlying need institution-wide unmet.

title: Find the correct York student-service information
statement: I need to locate the relevant student service so that I can take the next step on a University administrative question.
success: The user knows which questions SAVY can address and when a human service or another channel is needed.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The SAVY service page explains its role and limits; it does not replace an adviser.
action: Preserve the student-facing service explanation and reference it from the tool catalogue.

title: Find technical support for an AI service problem
statement: I need to reach support for an AI service problem so that I can get help through the appropriate service channel.
success: The user can identify the support/request route for the affected service.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: UIT publishes service support routes and SAVY has its own support context; the actual ticket workflows were not inspected.
action: Put the relevant support action on each service record; do not equate generic technical support with an AI-harm complaint process.

title: Obtain a non-AI learning route without disadvantage
statement: I need an appropriate non-AI alternative when AI use is proposed for learning so that my choice not to use it does not disadvantage me.
success: The user understands the choice principle and can identify how to arrange a suitable alternative in the relevant course.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: The educational choice principle explicitly supports alternatives, but a universal request/escalation process was not established in the reviewed guidance.
action: Add an actionable course-level request route and clarify where unresolved requests go.

title: Understand applicable York AI guidance in French
statement: I need to understand applicable York AI guidance in French so that language does not prevent me from finding the right answer.
success: A French-speaking user can reach equivalent, current guidance for the same core task.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: French SPARK routes were retrieved, but full French-language parity across policy explanations and tool tasks was not audited.
owner: Central web owner + bilingual content owners
action: Validate priority French-language needs and audit task-by-task parity before calling any translation absent.

title: Report harmful behaviour from a York AI service
statement: I need to report harmful behaviour from a York AI service so that an accountable owner can investigate it.
success: The user can identify a reporting route, required information and the responsible follow-up owner for AI-related harm.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Generic service support and ethical cautions were found, but no dedicated AI-harm reporting workflow was identified in the reviewed AI guidance. Another institutional process may exist outside the corpus.
owner: Proposed: hub owner + UIT + relevant equity/privacy/service owners
action: Confirm existing reporting processes and user demand; publish one scope-aware entry route if a gap is confirmed.

title: Know the immediate response to accidental disclosure through AI
statement: I need to know the immediate response after accidentally putting sensitive information into an AI tool so that the disclosure can be contained and assessed.
success: The user can identify whom to notify and the immediate approved steps for a suspected AI-related data disclosure.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Preventive data-handling guidance is present; an AI-specific first-response route was not identified in the reviewed AI content. Existing Information Security or privacy incident procedures may already cover this.
owner: Proposed: Information Security + privacy office + UIT support
action: Check the existing incident process first; surface its approved first-response instructions in the AI data task route.

title: Request human review of an AI-informed decision affecting me
statement: I need to request human review of an AI-informed decision that affects me so that I can challenge an inappropriate outcome.
success: The affected person can identify an applicable review/appeal route and its accountable human decision owner.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: Guidance requires human oversight and limits consequential uses, but no AI-specific affected-person recourse route was identified in the reviewed content. General academic/employment appeals may apply.
owner: Proposed: relevant decision owner + appropriate academic/administrative policy authority
action: Validate actual decision contexts and existing appeal processes before creating a new route; make applicable recourse discoverable.

title: Understand who coordinates York approach to AI
statement: I need to understand who coordinates York approach to AI so that I can locate the relevant institutional governance context.
success: The user can distinguish institutional coordination from the formal approval authority for a particular rule or tool.
validation: Analyst-inferred; not validated through user research
assessment: AI @ York explains the Roundtable, while UIT supplies an IT governance context. Neither should be assumed to approve every policy.
owner: Central AI web owner + relevant governance bodies
action: Publish a concise governance map distinguishing coordination, content ownership and formal approval.
